summary: Sliders for the settings an agent takes: a single slider with named stops (a Creativity slider from Precise to Creative, with a sample sentence that rewrites itself in the chosen tone), a stepped slider with a tick and a number at each step, and a range with two knobs that never cross. A value the agent recommends sits on the track as a mark you can press, and a knob dropped near it snaps to it.
use: For a setting with a few named levels that people understand better as words, like tone or effort.
For a whole number that moves in fixed steps, like tool calls or retries per run.
For a budget or a window with a lower and an upper bound.
When the agent can suggest a good value and you want people to see it without being forced to take it.
features: Drag a knob, or press anywhere on the track: the nearest knob comes to the pointer and follows it.
The value shows in the header beside the label, and changes as you drag, press a key or pick a stop.
`names` splits the range into named parts (Precise, Focused, Balanced, Playful, Creative); the nearest name shows beside the value.
`stops` adds buttons under the track that glide the knob to a value; `ticks` adds a tick and a number at each step, each one a button.

`recommended` draws the agent's mark over the track and a notch in it (in Clean, a 1px muted tick across the track). Pressing the mark glides the knob there, and a knob dragged within 5% of it snaps to it.
`description` is a line under the slider that crossfades when it changes, like a sample sentence in the chosen tone.
`RangeSlider` keeps its two knobs at least one step apart, so they can't cross; pressing the track moves the nearer knob.
`SliderGroup` is the panel they sit in on designme.dev, with a hairline between sliders. It grows and shrinks with what it holds, such as a description that changes length.

The track is a neutral grey and the part the knob covers is the accent's mark colour. The knob is white in Soft and Blueprint, in light and dark, and shows the focus ring only from the keyboard. In Clean the track is sunk (an inner shadow over it and its fill), the fill is white in dark mode, the knob is Clean's round monochrome knob (white in light, dark grey in dark) with a crisp hairline, and the agent's mark and its notch are grey. Clean's knob moves calmly: it glides at the style's pace, trails a drag by a short ease, and lifts on its shadow without the hop, the lean or the bounce.
a11y: Each knob has role="slider" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow, and an aria-valuetext with the unit and the name, like "0.40, Balanced, recommended" or "At most $0.35".
On a range, each knob's limits stop at the other knob, so a screen reader announces the real range.
The arrow keys move one step, Shift with an arrow or Page Up and Page Down move ten (or `bigStep`), and Home and End go to the ends.
Stops, ticks and the recommended mark are buttons, so they can be reached with Tab and pressed with Enter or Space; the mark has a label and a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus.
The keyboard focus ring is the quiet grey ring; a mouse or touch never shows one.

faq.q: How do I show the named stops without fixing the slider to them?
faq.a: Use `names` for the words and `step` for how finely it moves. The knob can sit anywhere; the name shown is the nearest one.

faq.q: Can I turn off the snapping to the recommended value?
faq.a: Snapping only happens when `recommended` is set. Leave it out and the knob moves freely by `step`.

faq.q: How do I format money or units?
faq.a: Pass `format`, for example `v => '$' + v.toFixed(2)`. It is used in the header and in the spoken value.
